title: Gershwin’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

entries.speaker: User
entries.text:
[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage. For composers outside the symphonic tradition it asks for an honest counterfactual.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.
notes: the pasted batch brief is summarised in brackets; the last sentence is verbatim

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — Gershwin’s Missing Symphony (work id gershwin-symphony-1)

Honest counterfactual: Gershwin wrote no symphony. His concert works are rhapsodies, a piano concerto, a tone poem, an overture and variations, and all but two of them have a solo piano. This piece imagines a short “Symphony in B flat” in three movements, fast–slow–fast like the Concerto in F, with the piano moved back into the orchestra. No theme is taken from Gershwin.

Orchestra (15 staves, sounding pitch): pairs of flutes, oboes, clarinets and bassoons, alto saxophone, four horns, three trumpets, three trombones and tuba, timpani, piano, strings. There is no drum kit, banjo or other percussion: the site’s player has no such sounds.

Language: melodies with flattened thirds and sevenths against major harmony (“blue notes”), chords of the sixth, ninth and thirteenth, the Charleston rhythm (a stab on the beat and another just before the third beat), walking basses, a twelve-bar blues. Because blue notes clash with the chords by design, the half-step and parallel-motion checks are switched off for this work.

Movements
I. Allegro, B flat: a syncopated clarinet theme over Charleston stabs; a broad tune in E flat; a short development with a piano break; reprise with the broad tune for full orchestra.
II. Blues: Andante con moto, E flat: a twelve-bar blues for trumpet, then alto saxophone with flute answers; a livelier middle in A flat; the blues for everyone.
III. Allegro agitato, B flat, 2/4: a rondo on a theme of hammered repeated notes, with the first movement’s theme, the blues and finally the broad tune returning between its statements.

Target length about eight minutes. What cannot be translated: swing. The player performs rhythms exactly as written, so the eighth notes are even. Compromise known from the start: tunes and chords are written by hand; a program writes the rhythm-section stabs, walking basses, piano figuration and full-orchestra textures from the chord plan.
